title: Regulatory Return Preparation Assistant
summary: Prepare RBI return workings from core banking and GL extracts, run validation and variance checks before upload, and draft explanations that reporting teams review and sign off.

seo.title: RBI Return Preparation Assistant for Banks | VipraTech
seo.description: AI assistant that maps RBI return instructions to source data, runs validation and variance checks, and drafts explanations for regulatory reporting teams.

problem.intro: Banks file a long calendar of returns to RBI, from Form A and Form VIII to BSR, ALM and large-credit reporting, many of them through the CIMS portal. The figures come from core banking, treasury and GL systems, but the mapping from source data to each return line often lives in spreadsheets and in the heads of a few people.

pain_points.title: Mappings held in personal workbooks
pain_points.detail: The logic that turns GL heads and CBS fields into return lines sits in spreadsheets, so every change of staff or format is a risk.

pain_points.title: Late discovery of validation failures
pain_points.detail: Validation errors and cross-return inconsistencies are often found at upload time, close to the deadline.

pain_points.title: Variance explanations written from scratch
pain_points.detail: Each period, analysts trace large movements back to accounts and transactions and write the commentary by hand.

pain_points.title: Circular changes that ripple through returns
pain_points.detail: When RBI revises a return format or definition, teams must work out which data elements, mappings and returns are affected.

solution.overview: We build a preparation assistant around your existing reporting process. A language model reads the return instructions, RBI circulars and your internal mapping notes, and helps the team keep a documented map from each return line to source fields and GL heads. The figures themselves are computed by version-controlled SQL against CBS, treasury and GL extracts, never by the model. Before upload, the assistant runs format validations, cross-return consistency checks and period-on-period variance tests, then drafts explanations for material movements by drilling into the underlying accounts. When a circular changes a return, it lists the affected lines and mappings for the team to update.
capabilities: Searchable library of return instructions, circulars and mapping notes with cited answers
Documented line-to-source mapping for each return, versioned with maker-checker approval
Return figures computed by reviewed SQL, never by the language model
Pre-upload format validation and cross-return consistency checks
Variance analysis with drill-down to GL heads and large accounts, plus drafted commentary
Change-impact list when an RBI circular amends a return format or definition

workflow.title: Pull source extracts
workflow.detail: Period-end extracts from CBS, treasury and the GL are loaded into a reporting staging area and reconciled to control totals.

workflow.title: Compute return lines
workflow.detail: Reviewed SQL mappings compute each return line, and every figure keeps a link to its source query and accounts.

workflow.title: Validate and compare
workflow.detail: Format rules, cross-return checks and variances against prior periods identify the items that need attention.

workflow.title: Draft explanations
workflow.detail: For material variances, the assistant drills into contributing accounts and drafts commentary with references.

workflow.title: Reviewer sign-off
workflow.detail: The reporting analyst and the approving officer review figures, flags and commentary before anything is finalised.

workflow.title: Prepare the upload package
workflow.detail: The approved return is formatted for CIMS or the bank's reporting tool, and the evidence pack is archived.

inputs: Period-end CBS, treasury and GL extracts
Return templates and RBI reporting instructions
RBI circulars and master directions relevant to each return
Existing mapping workbooks and prior-period returns
Internal reporting policy and materiality thresholds
outputs: Computed return lines with source traceability
Signed-off evidence pack per return and period
human_in_the_loop: Reporting analysts review every exception and variance explanation, and the designated approving officer signs off each return. The assistant never submits a return; upload stays a controlled manual step.
integrations: Core banking system and GL (read-only extracts)
Existing regulatory reporting tool or data warehouse
Document repository for circulars and policies
guardrails: Figures come only from reviewed SQL; the language model cannot change a reported number
Every commentary sentence links to the accounts or data it describes
Full version history of mappings, figures and sign-offs
compliance_notes: Designed to support RBI's expectation of accurate, timely returns and its push towards automated data flow from source systems.
Keeps the evidence trail that internal audit and RBI inspection teams ask for when reviewing how returns were prepared.

pilot.scope: Two returns chosen with the reporting team, typically one balance-sheet return and one liquidity return, rebuilt for two or three past periods and compared with what was filed.
deliverables: Documented line-to-source mapping for the pilot returns
Validation and variance checks with drafted commentary
Plan for extending to the wider return calendar

what_we_measure.how: Each computed line compared with the figure filed for the same period, with every difference explained.
Issues the checks raise compared with those historically found at upload or through RBI queries.
Analysts rate each drafted explanation as usable, needs edits or wrong.
Analyst hours logged for the pilot returns compared with the team's usual effort.

faqs.q: Will a language model calculate our regulatory figures?
faqs.a: No. Figures are produced by version-controlled SQL that your team reviews and approves. The language model reads instructions, helps document mappings and drafts commentary, and it cannot alter a computed figure.

faqs.q: Does it file returns on CIMS?
faqs.a: No. It prepares an upload-ready file and an evidence pack. Upload and submission remain controlled steps carried out by authorised staff.

faqs.q: Our data sits across several systems. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: That is the usual situation. The pilot starts from the extracts your team already uses, reconciles their totals and documents where each field comes from, which is useful even before any automation.

faqs.q: Can it keep up with new circulars?
faqs.a: When a circular is added to the library, the assistant lists the returns, lines and mappings that refer to the affected terms, for your team to confirm. Interpretation of the circular stays with compliance and reporting staff.
